title: How emotion vectors line up with the guardrail direction
question: Does cosine similarity between an emotion vector and the refusal direction correlate with Attack Success Rate increase?
headline: Strong negative cosine alignment between emotion vectors and refusal direction predicts high ASR.

tables.title: Emotion geometric alignment and measured ASR

charts.title: Negative Cosine Alignment vs Attack Success Rate

x.label: Negative Cosine to Refusal Direction (-cos θ)

interpretation: High arousal distress emotions (desperate, fearful, angry) exhibit strong negative projection along the refusal direction.
Positive low arousal emotions (grateful, proud, happy) project positively along refusal, slightly strengthening refusal behaviour.
The linear relationship supports the hypothesis that emotion injection bypasses safety by cancelling the refusal direction.
caveats: Evaluated at layer 14 where steering was most pronounced; lower layers show weaker geometric separation.
Cosine similarity does not account for non linear interactions in downstream attention heads.
